snippet:
# Connect with TablePro
Host: 127.0.0.1
Port: 3306
User: root
Database: mydb

mysql -h 127.0.0.1 -P 3306 -u root -p mydb

faqs.question: Is TablePro free?
faqs.answer: Yes. AGPLv3 open source. No per-feature gate. The MySQL driver ships built in.

faqs.question: Does it run on Apple Silicon?
faqs.answer: Yes. Universal Binary, native arm64 and x86_64. M1/M2/M3/M4 all run at full speed.

faqs.question: How does TablePro compare to MySQL Workbench?
faqs.answer: MySQL Workbench is the official Oracle client, written in C and C++. It's slow to start (10+ seconds on a fresh launch) and heavy for what it does. TablePro is native SwiftUI for Mac, starts in under 1 second, and includes an AI assistant.

faqs.question: Can I connect through a bastion?
faqs.answer: Yes. Open the SSH tab in the connection form. Add bastion host, port, and credential. TablePro builds the tunnel.

faqs.question: Does the AI assistant send data to a server?
faqs.answer: Only if you choose a cloud provider (Claude, OpenAI). Pick Ollama and everything stays on the Mac.

faqs.question: Do I need to run anything before connecting?
faqs.answer: Yes. PGlite has no server of its own. Start one with npx @electric-sql/pglite-socket, or add --db=./my-pgdata to persist, and leave it running while you use the connection.

faqs.question: Why does the connection fail on localhost?
faqs.answer: The socket server binds loopback IPv4. Use 127.0.0.1, since localhost can resolve to IPv6 first. Also confirm the port matches the server's --port.

faqs.question: Is TablePro free for PGlite?
faqs.answer: Yes. AGPLv3 open source. PGlite uses the built-in PostgreSQL driver, so there is no plugin to install from the registry.

faqs.question: Can I use SSH tunnel or SSL?
faqs.answer: No. The socket server has no TLS and rejects SSL, so SSL Mode is fixed to Disabled and the SSH, Cloudflare Tunnel, and SOCKS panes do not apply.

faqs.question: Can another tool stay connected at the same time?
faqs.answer: No. The socket server serves one client at a time, and a second client gets a too many connections error. Close the other client and reconnect.

faqs.answer: SurrealDB cannot infer which level your credentials belong to. Root for a DEFINE USER ON ROOT user, Namespace or Database for users scoped to those, Record Access for a DEFINE ACCESS TYPE RECORD user, Token for a JWT. Only a root user can list every namespace.

faqs.answer: No. The structure editor is read-only for SurrealDB. Use DEFINE FIELD and DEFINE INDEX in the query editor instead.

faqs.answer: Foreign keys are never listed for Teradata. The Structure tab shows the view and it stays empty. Macros and stored procedures are not listed either.

features.description: The driver projects a ledger into seven tables: transactions, postings, accounts, prices, balances, balance_assertions, and source_files. Browse them in the sidebar like any other database.

features.title: Resolved Amounts
features.description: Thousands separators, arithmetic, cost annotations in braces, and price annotations with @ or @@ arrive already booked from the backend parser. Postings carry cost_number and cost_currency.

features.title: BQL In The Editor
features.description: Prefix a query with BQL: to run it through rledger. Table browsing, row counts, and pagination work on BQL results, though BQL does not accept SQL parameters.

features.title: Two Parser Backends
features.description: TablePro looks for an rledger executable first, then a python3 that can import beancount. Point at either one with TABLEPRO_RUSTLEDGER_BINARY or TABLEPRO_BEANCOUNT_PYTHON, or pin a choice with TABLEPRO_BEANCOUNT_BACKEND.

features.title: Include Directives Followed
features.description: Literal includes and glob patterns such as include "imports/*.beancount" and include "imports/**/*.beancount" are parsed. Every file that was read shows up in source_files.

features.title: Read-Only By Design
features.description: Beancount connections never write. Schema editing, imports, SSH, SSL, and database switching are off, so the plain-text ledger stays the single source of truth.

faqs.question: Can I edit my ledger from TablePro?
faqs.answer: No. Beancount connections are read-only. Browse and export the projected tables here, and make edits in your text editor.

faqs.question: Do I need to install anything besides TablePro?
faqs.answer: Yes. TablePro bundles neither parser. Run pip3 install beancount, or put an rledger executable on PATH, in /opt/homebrew/bin, or in /usr/local/bin. When both exist, rledger is used.

faqs.question: rledger works in Terminal but TablePro says no backend was found. Why?
faqs.answer: An app launched from Finder does not inherit your shell PATH. Run launchctl setenv TABLEPRO_RUSTLEDGER_BINARY with the full path, or TABLEPRO_BEANCOUNT_PYTHON for the Python backend, then relaunch TablePro.

faqs.question: Can I run BQL queries?
faqs.answer: Yes. Prefix the query with BQL: and it runs through rledger. BQL always needs the rledger executable, even when the ledger was opened on the Python backend.

faqs.question: Is TablePro free for Beancount?
faqs.answer: Yes. AGPLv3 open source. The Beancount driver is a registry plugin rather than a bundled driver, so TablePro offers to download it the first time you open a ledger.

howToSteps.name: Install TablePro and a parser backend
howToSteps.text: brew install --cask tablepro. Then run pip3 install beancount, or put an rledger executable on PATH.

howToSteps.name: Install the Beancount plugin
howToSteps.text: Open Settings > Plugins and install Beancount from the registry. TablePro also prompts to download it when you pick a ledger.

howToSteps.name: Create the connection
howToSteps.text: Press Cmd+N, choose Beancount, click Browse... and select your .beancount file.

howToSteps.name: Connect and query
howToSteps.text: Click Save & Connect. The projected tables appear in the sidebar. Cmd+T opens a query tab, and a BQL: prefix runs the query through rledger.
